checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add a structural and byte-level score comparison command

impact_assessment.why: After variation and transposition there can be many similar scores; telling what actually changed requires a repeatable comparison.
impact_assessment.benefits: compare reports structural differences and whether the rendered audio is byte-identical, in a stable ordering suitable for tests and scripts.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: compare must be read-only, never fail on differences, and keep exact output ordering; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure compare module with exact-vector tests and a CLI command reading two score files, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 90 tests green; compare output pinned byte-for-byte for identical and differing scores
Task 'coda-compare' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add MIDI import for the type-0 subset Coda exports

impact_assessment.why: Coda could write MIDI but not read it back, so an exported piece could not be edited or compared as a score again.
impact_assessment.benefits: import-midi reconstructs tempo, pitches, timing and velocities from a single-track MIDI file, closing the symbolic round-trip.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: unsupported formats or running-status violations must fail with a clear message and never panic; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Write a bounds-checked parser with error tests, add byte-vector round-trip tests through export then import, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 96 tests green; supported-subset MIDI round-trip preserves byte-identical audio and richer scores report their non-MIDI losses via compare
Task 'coda-midi-import' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: af500fa90af051f7adf20d9f480fd61fdffc6014

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add format-1 multi-track MIDI import

impact_assessment.why: Real MIDI files from DAWs are usually format 1 with a tempo track and separate note tracks; Coda only accepted format 0.
impact_assessment.benefits: Notes from all tracks merge into one deterministic Score while tempo meta events are honored from any track.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: existing format-0 imports must stay byte-identical; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Refactor track parsing to return notes and tempo separately, merge and sort deterministically, add a multi-track byte fixture test, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 99 tests green; format-1 conductor and note tracks merge into one score with tempo and deterministic note order
Task 'coda-multitrack-midi' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: c0c0717051fdaa82f4852184d83f189fb16d6c63

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add WAV joining across multiple scores

impact_assessment.why: Long pieces are written as sections, but Coda could only render one score per file; joining renders a sequence as one WAV.
impact_assessment.benefits: join validates sample-rate parity and concatenates PCM data with a corrected RIFF header, so sections compose without external audio tools.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: individual WAV bytes and golden vectors must not change; mismatched sample rates must fail clearly; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure join module with exact header/data byte tests, a CLI command rendering each input at one rate, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 104 tests green; joined WAV header and concatenated data pinned byte-for-byte, mixed sample rates rejected
Task 'coda-join' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: 5ee1ed12177abeb2702db6dd9dc398d766746062

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add a deterministic score statistics command

impact_assessment.why: Scores are now generated, varied, imported and joined; a quick summary is needed to compare them without reading the source.
impact_assessment.benefits: stats reports counts, duration, pitch range, distinct pitches, density, waveforms and pan span in a stable format suitable for scripts and tests.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: stats must be read-only with exact, ordered output and safe behavior on empty scores; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure stats module with exact-string tests including the empty case, a CLI command reusing score loading, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 108 tests green; stats output pinned byte-for-byte including empty-score safety
Task 'coda-stats' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add deterministic WAV peak normalization

impact_assessment.why: Rendered and joined WAVs can be too quiet; a local normalization step makes levels usable without external audio tools.
impact_assessment.benefits: normalize scales a Coda WAV to a chosen peak with deterministic clamping and is idempotent, so it can be re-run safely.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: non-WAV or silent input must be handled without divide-by-zero or panic; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure normalize module with exact peak, idempotence and silence tests, a CLI command, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 113 tests green; normalization peak, idempotence and silence handling pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-normalize' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add built-in score templates

impact_assessment.why: A blank score is a slow starting point; named templates give composers a deterministic sketch to render, vary or edit.
impact_assessment.benefits: templates lists the sketches and template <name> materializes one as canonical source, reusing the parser and serializer.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: every template must parse and re-serialize exactly; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Store templates as parseable source strings with a lookup API, add exact-list and round-trip tests, a CLI command, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 117 tests green; template listing exact and every template parses, renders and re-serializes identically
